title: Waste stream separation and lawful disposal
audience: Garden, lawn, irrigation and landscape crews and supervisors who collect, load, transport and dispose of green waste and other site material.
learningOutcomes: Separate clean green waste, diseased or invasive plant matter, treated timber, chemicals and sharps at the point of collection.
Confirm that a disposal destination accepts each waste stream before the load leaves the site.
Load and secure waste so that it does not blow, leak or enter drains.
Complete a waste record that supports the client's handover and any audit.

instruction.heading: Why waste separation saves money and protects sites
instruction.body: A garden clean-up produces several kinds of waste, and each kind has its own handling and disposal route. Clean green waste such as lawn clippings, small prunings and leaves usually goes to a green-waste facility. Diseased or invasive plant matter may need to be contained, treated or sent to a specified destination. Treated timber, chemical containers, paint tins, batteries and sharps are not general green waste. When these streams are mixed, the whole load can be rejected at the gate, the crew may pay for a second trip, and a contaminated load can spread disease or chemicals. Separation at the source is faster and cheaper than sorting at the disposal site. It is also one of the simplest ways to show the client that the job was done properly. Waste separation depends on knowing what is in the load, so the first step is always a site walk to identify the waste types before collection begins.

instruction.heading: Sorting at the point of collection
instruction.body: Set up separate, labelled containers before collection starts. Use one container or pile for clean green waste, one for diseased or suspect plant matter, one for treated timber, and one for any chemical or sharps item that the business is authorised to handle. Keep the chemicals and sharps out of general containers altogether, and do not compact them into a bin with clippings. If a chemical container is leaking or unlabelled, do not open it. Move the container to a safe, ventilated, contained area, and stop until the supervisor confirms the product and the handling route. Treated timber is often not accepted in green-waste streams. Keep it apart, and confirm its acceptance at the destination before it is loaded. Sharp items, such as broken glass, needles and metal, need puncture-resistant containers and a clear label. Do not hand-sort mixed heaps. Use tools and a defined work area to reduce contact with hazards.

instruction.heading: Confirming destinations and rules
instruction.body: Before loading a vehicle, confirm where each waste stream is going. Ask the disposal facility what it accepts, whether it requires a manifest or booking, whether it will accept diseased or invasive material, and whether it has a separate stream for treated timber, liquids and sharps. Write the answers down with the date and the name of the person who gave them. Acceptance rules and the rules for transporting regulated waste differ between states, territories and local councils, and this draft does not confirm them for any particular location. Where a waste type is regulated, such as certain liquids, asbestos-containing material or hazardous chemicals, the crew must not handle it under this lesson. Stop, contain the area, and refer it to the supervisor and to a licence holder or specialist service. Do not guess a destination, and do not send mixed loads to a facility that has not confirmed it will accept them.

instruction.heading: Loading, transport and records
instruction.body: Load each stream into the correct vehicle or container, and secure it so that it cannot shift, blow or leak in transit. Use a cover or net for loose material, and check the load before the vehicle leaves the property. Keep loads off the kerb or footpath, and do not let material enter the stormwater system. Make a waste record for every load. Record the date, the site, the waste types and estimated volumes, the container or vehicle used, the destination, the time of arrival, and the receipt or ticket number. If anything goes wrong, such as a spill, a leaking container or a rejected load, record it and inform the supervisor. The waste record is part of the job's evidence, and it should be handed over with the final inspection described in the handover lesson.

instruction.heading: Verification and escalation
instruction.body: A supervisor should check the sorting decisions as well as the paperwork. A competent worker can point to each stream on a site, explain why a stream is kept apart, name the destination that accepts it and show the receipt. Escalate immediately when a container is leaking, a chemical is unlabelled, sharps are mixed into a green-waste load, or a destination will not confirm acceptance. Do not hide a rejected load or send it somewhere else without authority. Record the rejection and the decision that followed.

procedure: Walk the site and list each waste type that is expected, noting any chemical, treated timber, sharps or suspect plant matter.
Set up labelled, separate containers or piles for each waste stream before collection starts.
Collect clean green waste first and keep it separate from every other stream.
Stop and refer any leaking, unlabelled or unknown chemical container before touching it.
Confirm the acceptance rules and the destination for each stream, and record the answers with the name and date.
Load each stream into the correct vehicle or container, and secure and cover loose material.
Check the load before departure and make sure no material is on the kerb, footpath or near a drain.
Record the waste types, volumes, destination and receipt, and hand the record to the supervisor.

workedExamples.situation: The trailer contains grass clippings, diseased branches, a piece of treated pine and a leaking spray container that a client has put on the pile.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How should the crew handle the trailer and the container before the load leaves the site?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop loading. Do not compact or cover the leaking container. Move it to a safe, ventilated, contained area and inform the supervisor, who confirms the product and whether the business is authorised to handle it. Separate the diseased branches from the clippings, confirm the destination for the diseased material, and keep the treated pine apart until its acceptance is confirmed. Record each decision. Do not send the mixed trailer to a green-waste facility.

workedExamples.situation: A crew is cutting back a shrub and finds broken glass and a used needle in the root ball.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do the sharps change the disposal route?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop handling the mixed pile by hand. Use tools to move the material and place sharp items in a puncture-resistant container with a clear label, kept apart from green waste. Confirm with the supervisor whether the business is authorised to handle needles, and if not, refer the needle to a specialist service. Record the item and the decision.

equipmentAndPpe: Puncture-resistant gloves rated for sharps handling
Eye protection when working with debris
Labelled containers for green waste, diseased material, treated timber and sharps
Covers, nets and tarps for loads
Waste record sheet or digital equivalent

commonErrors.error: Mixing treated timber, sharps or chemicals into a green-waste load.
commonErrors.prevention: Separate at collection. Keep each stream in its own labelled container and confirm the destination for each.

commonErrors.error: Assuming the disposal facility will sort a mixed load.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm acceptance in advance. A facility may reject the whole load, and the crew may pay for a second trip.

commonErrors.error: Leaving a loose load uncovered on the trailer, which blows onto the road or into a drain.
commonErrors.prevention: Cover and secure every load, and check the load before departure.

commonErrors.error: Writing a receipt that does not match the waste types actually loaded.
commonErrors.prevention: Record each stream and volume at the time of loading and match the receipt to the record before filing it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Waste acceptance rules, transport requirements, manifest or booking requirements and the rules for treated timber, liquids and sharps vary by state, territory and local council.

Handling, transporting or disposing of some waste types, including hazardous chemicals and asbestos-containing material, may need a licence, a permit or an approved handler. This lesson does not grant any licence or permit and does not authorise the crew to handle those materials.

Asbestos-containing material, such as older fibre-cement sheeting that may be found in garden sheds or fences, must not be broken, cut or cleared by the crew. In Victoria, only a Class A licence holder may remove friable asbestos, and a clearance certificate is required if any quantity of friable asbestos was involved (Asbestos Victoria, removing or disposing of asbestos page; labelled Updated, no date shown). The Victorian allowance for unlicensed removal covers non-friable material only: no more than 10 square metres in total and no more than one hour of removal work in any seven days (Asbestos Victoria, unlicensed asbestos removal page; labelled Updated, no date shown). Check the licence position for each state or territory with the relevant regulator before relying on it. Stop, contain and refer.

Under the model Work Health and Safety framework, duty holders must manage the risks of handling and transporting waste so far as is reasonably practicable, including the risk of material falling from a vehicle.

qualityStandard: Each waste stream is separated at the point of collection and kept in a labelled container or pile.
Each load has a confirmed destination that accepts the stream, recorded with the name of the person who confirmed it.
No load leaves the site uncovered or mixed with a stream it is not approved to carry.
Each load has a waste record that matches the loaded material and the receipt.
documentationEvidence: Waste stream plan for the job, listing expected waste types and containers.
Destination confirmation record with the date, the facility name and the person who gave the answer.
Load record for each vehicle or container, with the time, the site, the waste types, the estimated volumes and the receipt number.
Incident and rejection record for any leak, spill, unlabelled container or refused load.
summary: Separate waste at the point of collection. Green waste, diseased or invasive matter, treated timber, chemicals and sharps are kept apart.
Confirm where each stream goes and whether it is accepted before the load leaves the site.
Cover and secure every load, and keep material off roads, footpaths and drains.
Stop and refer any chemical, sharps mix or suspected asbestos. This lesson does not grant authority to handle regulated waste.

knowledgeChecks.question: A trailer load contains clean clippings, treated timber and sharps. What is the correct approach?
options: Keep each stream separate and confirm the destination for each before loading.
Take the whole load to the green-waste facility and let them sort it.
Load the old fencing with the clippings to save trips

knowledgeChecks.question: The disposal facility has not confirmed it will accept a particular stream. What should the crew do?
options: Take the load anyway and ask at the gate and the staff there will sort it out
Hold the stream, record the unconfirmed destination and refer the decision to the supervisor.
Leave the stream at the roadside for council collection and do not record the stream at all

knowledgeChecks.question: A worker finds broken fibre-cement sheeting in an old shed during a clean-up. What is the correct action?
options: Break the sheets into smaller pieces so they fit in the bin and then bag them with the green waste for collection on Friday
Sweep up the dust with a broom and include it in the green waste and then hose the area down with the rest of the rubbish
Stop, contain the area, do not break or cut the material, and refer it to the supervisor and a licence holder or specialist service.
